title: Yutu-2 panoramic camera images archive (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.11150203, CC BY 4.0)
description: An 11.79 GB openly-licensed archive of Yutu-2 rover panoramic camera images plus a classified-crater dataset, deposited on Zenodo to accompany a study of impact-crater degradation in Yutu-2's rovering area. Contains a large PCAM photogrammetric product measured at 27308 x 21804 px (~595 megapixels).
format: ZIP archive (contains imagery + a large raster product)
credit: Ma, Xinyu; Chen, Meixi; Hu, Teng (2024) - 'Study on the degradation pattern of impact crater communities in Yutu-2's rovering area', Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.11150203
licence: CC BY 4.0, access_right 'open'. Verified in BOTH the Zenodo API ("license":{"id":"cc-by-4.0"}) and DataCite (rightsIdentifier 'cc-by-4.0', rightsIdentifierScheme 'SPDX', rightsUri https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode). Attribution required.
notes: VERIFIED by me via the Zenodo API and api.datacite.org. Record: title 'Study on the degradation pattern of impact crater communities in Yutu-2's rovering area', publication_date 2024-05-08, state 'findable'. Files exactly: 'Classified Craters.zip' (6538131 B, md5 f68b26755ad092fa705e6a8c7fbd65b5) and "Yutu 2 rover's panoramic camera captures images.zip" (11794265870 B = 11.79 GB, md5 a28dfb0a811ff836dc6af465a704b633). The 27308 x 21804 dimension was measured by a subagent (its BigTIFF-aware reader) on a raster product inside the archive - I confirmed the record metadata, licence and file sizes but did NOT re-measure the raster myself. RISK IS 'MEDIUM' not 'low': this is a DEPOSITOR'S SELF-APPLIED CC BY 4.0 over upstream CNSA/CLEP data, so third-party rights in the source imagery may still subsist and the depositor may not have had the authority to license it. This is nevertheless the strongest machine-readable licence attached to actual CE-4 PCAM imagery found anywhere, and it is 11.79 GB of it.

title: Chang'e 3 lander TCAM Level-2C stitched panorama, 2013-12-17 (highest-resolution CE-3 panorama found)
description: The highest-resolution single Chang'e panorama found anywhere in this research: a 15743 x 3505 stitch of the Chang'e 3 lander terrain camera (TCAM) Level-2C colour products, from the 2013-12-17 imaging sequence. Wider than the CE-4 IAU panorama (10000 px). Mirrored by The Planetary Society carrying CNSA/CLEP data.
credit: CNSA / CLEP, Chang'e 3 TCAM; mirrored by The Planetary Society. Product id encoded in the filename: TCAM-I-001_SCI_P_20131217113548_0004_A_2C_stitch.
licence: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 (per The Planetary Society). The NC clause forbids use in a monetised demo; the ND clause forbids derivative works, which includes reprojecting this panorama into a Three.js equirectangular skybox.
notes: MEASURED by me: 206 | JPEG | 15743x3505 | 15302339 bytes (14.59 MB). This CORRECTS my initial finding that no high-resolution CE-3 panorama exists. LICENCE IS THE BLOCKER: although it is a Creative Commons licence, NC+ND make it unusable for a monetised demo and for reprojection. Three further CE-3 mosaics were subagent-reported (8192x5293, 4095x2768, 2144x2144) but I did not re-measure those. No degree coverage is stated by the source; 360 is inferred from the series being a ring panorama, so treat it as an inference.

title: Chang'e 3 complete raw PCAM/TCAM archive (The Planetary Society mirror, no login)
description: Complete raw Chang'e 3 rover PCAM and lander TCAM frame archive mirrored by The Planetary Society, downloadable without login. Frames measure 2352 x 1728 PNG.
credit: CNSA / CLEP, via The Planetary Society
licence: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 (per The Planetary Society)
notes: Subagent-reported (URL and 2352x1728 frame size). I did not personally probe these index pages. Non-commercial + no-derivatives, so same NC/ND blocker as the 15743 px panorama. Useful as a research/derivation source but not shippable as-is.

title: Chang'e 5 lander+ascender PCAM ring panorama with the national flag (CNSA, 4 Dec 2020)
description: Official CNSA Chang'e 5 surface panorama, imaged by the panoramic camera on the lander/ascender combination, showing the five-star red flag unfurled on the lunar surface plus the sampling arm and sampler. Published 2020-12-04. This resolves the previously unexplained 7500x4053 file.
credit: China National Space Administration (国家航天局), 2020-12-04
licence: All rights reserved. Site footer states only '版权所有：国家航天局 承办单位：国家航天局新闻宣传中心'. No open licence, no reuse grant, no CC statement.
notes: MEASURED by me: 206 | JPEG | 7500x4053 | 24758565 bytes. This is byte-identical to the previously unattributed local file. Source page title: '国家航天局公布嫦娥五号月表国旗展示照片'; caption verbatim: '嫦娥五号着陆器和上升器组合体全景相机环拍成像，五星红旗在月面成功展开，此外图像上方可见已完成表取采样的机械臂及采样器。' So CE-5 DID publish an official surface panorama. Bye-identical CLEP mirror: http://www.clep.org.cn/n5982341/c6810754/part/6785492.jpg . GEOMETRY: CNSA states only '全景相机环拍成像' (panoramic-camera pan-around imaging) - NO projection and NO degree coverage stated. The image is a fan/sector-shaped stitched mosaic with large black unfilled corners in a 1.85:1 frame: NOT equirectangular, NOT a 2:1 360x180 strip, NOT a cylindrical 360 strip. Do not attach a degree figure. Carries a burned-in 中国探月/CLEP watermark. REFERENCE-ONLY. No VSSO CC BY 4.0 record exists for any CE-5 PCAM dataset, so CE-5 has no open-licence route.

title: Chang'e 6 lander PCAM stitched panoramic image - CNSA master (800x421, 4 June 2024)
description: The CNSA original of the official Chang'e 6 stitched panoramic image taken with the panoramic camera on the lander during surface sampling, showing Chaffee crater to the north and the landing legs and compressed regolith below. This 800x421 file is the true master; the widely-mirrored 1024 px copies are padded upscales.
credit: China National Space Administration (国家航天局), 2024-06-04
licence: All rights reserved. CNSA site footer carries no reuse grant and no CC statement.
notes: MEASURED by me: 206 | JPEG | 800x421 | 40868 bytes. Caption verbatim: '该图由全景相机在嫦娥六号表取采样前，对着陆点北侧月面拍摄的彩色图像镶嵌制作而成。图像上方是着陆点北部查菲环形山，图像的下方是着陆腿和着陆时冲击挤压隆起的月壤。' CORRECTION to my earlier report: I first recorded the CE-6 panorama as 1024x539 from People's Daily; the true master is 800x421 and the 1024 px copies are padded upscales (same 1.90:1 aspect; a subagent confirmed this visually). So the official CE-6 panorama is even smaller than first reported - far too small to be a hero asset. Bye-identical CLEP mirror: http://www.clep.org.cn/n5982014/c10707551/part/10707557.jpg . Sharpest CE-6 material is elsewhere: three LCAM descent frames at 2352x1728 (part/10543420-22.jpg) and a 1280x800 lander+ascender selfie (part/10543450.jpg).

title: Chang'e 3 / Yutu PCAM mosaic of boulders near Ziwei crater (open-access paper figure, CC BY 4.0)
description: Mosaic obtained by the panoramic camera on the Yutu rover showing metre-scale boulders excavated by Ziwei crater. Published as a figure in an open-access journal article, which is why it carries a genuine CC BY 4.0 licence rather than agency terms.
credit: Chunyu Ding, Zhiyong Xiao, Yan Su et al. - DOI 10.1186/s40623-021-01359-7 (Earth, Planets and Space)
licence: CC BY 4.0 - true open licence, no NC, no ND. Attribution required.
notes: VERIFIED by me via the Commons imageinfo API: size 265094, 1594x646, LicenseShortName 'CC BY 4.0', UsageTerms 'Creative Commons Attribution 4.0', AttributionRequired 'true', License 'cc-by-4.0'. Description: 'Abundant meter-scale boulders have been excavated by the Ziwei crater... This mosaic was obtained by the panoramic camera on the Yutu rover.' Real Chang'e 3 surface pixels under a clean open licence - but small and partial coverage, not a full panorama. STRATEGY NOTE: open-access papers publishing Chang'e figures under CC BY are the most legally robust route to real surface imagery and are worth systematic mining.

title: Chang'e 6 PCAM image of the scooped sampling area (open-access paper figure, CC BY 4.0)
description: Image of the scooped sampling area on the lunar surface captured by the Chang'e 6 panoramic camera, published as a figure in an open-access journal article.
credit: Chunlai Li, Hao Hu, Meng-Fei Yang et al. - DOI 10.1093/nsr/nwae328 (National Science Review)
licence: CC BY 4.0 - true open licence, no NC, no ND. Attribution required.
notes: VERIFIED by me via the Commons imageinfo API: size 300703, 804x682, LicenseShortName 'CC BY 4.0', AttributionRequired 'true'. Description: 'Image of the scooped area on the lunar surface captured by the Chang'e-6 panoramic camera.' This is the only cleanly-licensed real CE-6 surface image found; small and partial, not a panorama. WARNING: the Commons file 'Chang-e-5-Lander-Flag.png' (1620x1080, also CC BY 4.0) is an artist's CGI impression, NOT a photograph - do not present it as real imagery. The CE-6 flag photograph remains UNVERIFIED (its only host was unreachable), so it has no confirmed URL or dimensions.

title: Chang'e 4 S1 360-degree PCAM ring panorama, cylindrical projection (GRAS education gallery)
description: Stitched 360-degree ring-shot panorama taken by the panoramic camera on the Yutu-2 rover at waypoint S1. Shows the lander on the surface with solar panels deployed, the rover's own shadow, the PCAM mast and the rover's wheel tracks. Unique - this file is not on Wikimedia Commons or the IAU archive. Served as a plain unauthenticated JPEG from the GRAS education gallery.
credit: CNSA / CLEP, Ground Research and Application System (GRAS), NAOC. Required credit per NSSDC record.
licence: CC BY 4.0 per NSSDC/VSSO registry record 1240 (datasetId b2064561-01e2-4b11-bec0-a09502efd9af, DOI 10.12176/03.88.00007, CSTR 14804.11.03.88.00007, shareScope 完全共享 'fully shared'). NOTE: the GRAS platform itself separately publishes an all-rights-reserved copyright notice.
notes: MEASURED by me: 206 | JPEG | 10000x833 | 6228953 bytes, reached via the unauthenticated endpoint GET https://moon.bao.ac.cn/moon-admin/client/education/educationList?pageNum=1&pageSize=100&task=7&load=372 (task=7 Chang'e 4, load=372 PCAM). CRITICAL CAVEAT: the file carries a BAKED-IN VISIBLE WATERMARK which I confirmed by cropping the top-right corner at full resolution and viewing it - a '中国探月 CLEP' logo plus a '地面应用系统 GRAS' logo (the latter clipped by the image edge). CC BY 4.0 does not entitle you to remove it; budget for keeping it. The gallery lists TWO S1 entries labelled 方位投影 (azimuthal) and 圆柱投影 (cylindrical); they are BYTE-IDENTICAL (same sha256, both 10000x833 / 6,228,953 B), so only ONE S1 panorama exists and it is cylindrical - the gallery's own title/filename disagree, so trust the measured geometry over the label. URL must be percent-encoded (Chinese characters + full-width parentheses in the filename).

title: Chang'e 4 A-point triple-ring mosaic, cylindrical projection - the famous farside panorama (GRAS education gallery)
description: 360-degree ring-shot mosaic of the Chang'e 4 landing site at waypoint A, assembled from three ring-shot passes by the lander's terrain camera (TCAM). This is the scene of the famous January/February 2019 farside panorama release. Shows the lander deck with deployed solar panels and the Yutu-2 rover at mid-distance with its wheel tracks.
credit: CNSA / CLEP, Ground Research and Application System (GRAS), NAOC
licence: CC BY 4.0 per NSSDC/VSSO registry record 1302 (TCAM image gallery, DOI 10.12176/03.88.00006). GRAS platform separately publishes an all-rights-reserved notice.
notes: MEASURED by me: 206 | JPEG | 10000x1229 | 1894270 bytes. I DOWNLOADED AND VIEWED this file: it is a genuine full cylindrical sweep of the CE-4 landing site (lander deck with solar panels, Yutu-2 at mid-distance with wheel tracks, black sky). It is the SAME SCENE as the IAU iau1901a file, which has identical dimensions (10000x1229) - so the IAU copy is the same panorama. PREFER THE IAU COPY: 3,346,126 B vs 1,894,270 B at identical dimensions (less compression) and NO WATERMARK. This GRAS file has a baked-in visible watermark ('中国探月 CLEP' + '地面应用系统 GRAS'), which I confirmed by cropping and viewing the top-right corner at full resolution. GRAS's own description reads: '当月球车行驶到A点时，地形地貌相机进行了360度环拍成像，该图由三次环拍图像镶嵌而成，投影方式为圆柱投影' (when the rover reached point A the terrain camera performed 360-degree ring imaging; this image is a mosaic of three ring-shot images, cylindrical projection).

title: Chang'e 4 A-point triple-ring mosaic, azimuthal projection (little planet)
description: The same A-point 360-degree ring-shot mosaic rendered in azimuthal (fisheye/stereographic) projection - a 'little planet' view of the Chang'e 4 landing site.
credit: CNSA / CLEP, Ground Research and Application System (GRAS), NAOC
licence: CC BY 4.0 per NSSDC/VSSO registry record 1302 (DOI 10.12176/03.88.00006).
notes: MEASURED by me: 206 | JPEG | 5000x4915 | 3039109 bytes; I also downloaded it. Azimuthal projection is a near-circular disk - convenient for a spherical cap or a hero image, but NOT directly usable as an equirectangular skybox. Carries the same baked-in CLEP/GRAS watermark.

title: Chang'e 4 D-point triple-ring mosaics, azimuthal and cylindrical
description: 360-degree ring-shot mosaics of the Chang'e 4 landing site at waypoint D by the lander terrain camera, in azimuthal and cylindrical projections.
credit: CNSA / CLEP, Ground Research and Application System (GRAS), NAOC
licence: CC BY 4.0 per NSSDC/VSSO registry record 1302 (DOI 10.12176/03.88.00006).
notes: The azimuthal file is MEASURED by me at 206 | JPEG | 5000x4879 | 4614955 bytes. Its cylindrical sibling is a separate file: https://moon.bao.ac.cn/img-api/upload/www/201911/7D%E7%82%B9%E4%B8%89%E5%9C%88%E9%95%B6%E5%B5%8C%E5%9B%BE%EF%BC%88%E5%9C%86%E6%9F%B1%E6%8A%95%E5%BD%B1%EF%BC%89.jpg , MEASURED by me at 206 | JPEG | 5000x687 | 3609970 bytes. Note the cylindrical D-point file is only 687 px tall (a very thin strip) - lower quality than the A-point cylindrical. Both carry the baked-in CLEP/GRAS watermark. Width/height/byteSize fields in this record describe the azimuthal file.

title: Chang'e 4 PCAM mosaics of the lander from waypoints A, D and S1
description: Three multi-frame panoramic-camera mosaics imaging the Chang'e 4 lander itself from rover waypoints A, D and S1. The A-point image is a 6-frame mosaic; the D-point image shows the national flag; the S1 image shows the low-frequency radio spectrometer antenna.
credit: CNSA / CLEP, Ground Research and Application System (GRAS), NAOC
licence: CC BY 4.0 per NSSDC/VSSO registry record 1240 (DOI 10.12176/03.88.00007, shareScope 完全共享).
notes: MEASURED by me, all three: S1 -> 206 | JPEG | 5397x3157 | 5358411 bytes (this downloadUrl); A -> 200 | JPEG | 5638x3113 | 2655851 bytes at https://moon.bao.ac.cn/img-api/upload/2026/07/21/1A%E7%82%B9%E6%8B%8D%E7%9D%80%E9%99%86%E5%99%A8_20260721085708A262.jpg ; D -> 200 | JPEG | 5691x3179 | 1895578 bytes at https://moon.bao.ac.cn/img-api/upload/2026/07/21/2D%E7%82%B9%E6%8B%8D%E7%9D%80%E9%99%86%E5%99%A8_20260721085750A264.jpg . Width/height/byteSize fields describe the S1 file. GRAS description for A: '巡视器行驶到A点，搭载的全景相机对着陆器成像。该图像由6幅影像数据镶嵌制作而成' (6-frame mosaic). Not 360-degree panoramas - these are lander-portrait mosaics, useful as secondary/context imagery. Carry the baked-in CLEP/GRAS watermark.

title: Chang'e 4 PCAM quick-view frames, lunar days 1-9 (the NSSDC 全景相机图片集)
description: The set of PCAM quick-view surface frames from Yutu-2 covering lunar days 1-9, including wheel tracks, rocks, craters and the 'colour photos' of lunar day 9. This is the concrete deliverable behind the NSSDC/VSSO record 1240 'Panoramic camera image galleries' and the SMOC release announcement of 2020-07-27 (27 images).
credit: CNSA / CLEP, Ground Research and Application System (GRAS), NAOC
licence: CC BY 4.0 per NSSDC/VSSO registry record 1240 (DOI 10.12176/03.88.00007, shareScope 完全共享 'fully shared').
notes: MEASURED by me across the whole gallery (48 items enumerated via GET /moon-admin/client/education/educationList?task=7&load=372): most quick-view frames are 1176x865 or 1176x864; the three '月背彩照' (lunar-day-9 colour photos) are 2352x1730, e.g. CE4_PCAM_0901.jpg / 0902 / 0903. The downloadUrl above is the first frame (1176x865, 131875 bytes). Filenames follow CE4_PCAM_DDNN.jpg where DD = lunar day and NN = frame index. NOTE these are quick-look renditions, not the full-resolution raw PCAM frames (see ce4-gras-pcam-2b-frame, 1176x864 raw) - and they carry the baked-in CLEP/GRAS watermark.

title: The first panorama from the far side of the moon (Chang'e 4 landing site, IAU image iau1901a)
description: Cylindrical panorama of the Chang'e 4 landing site in Von Karman crater, far side of the Moon. Author CNSA; distributed by the International Astronomical Union as image iau1901a, release date 2019-02-15. This is the only full-surface Chang'e panorama found that is both high-resolution and openly licensed.
credit: CNSA / CLEP, via International Astronomical Union (IAU image iau1901a)
licence: CC BY 4.0 (Wikimedia raw wikitext: {{IAU-source|iau1901a}} and {{cc-by-4.0|CNSA}})
notes: MEASURED by me: 206 | JPEG | 10000x1229 | 3346126 bytes, via HTTP Range GET + JPEG SOF parse. Wikimedia file page states 'Original file (10,000 x 1,229 pixels, file size: 3.19 MB, MIME type: image/jpeg)' and category 'CC-BY-4.0'. GEOMETRY CAVEAT: ~8.14:1 cylindrical strip, NOT 2:1 equirectangular - vertical padding/remapping required before use as a Three.js skybox. The '360 degree' coverage comes from the CNSA/Xinhua release framing (huanpai 'ring-shot', azimuthal+cylindrical projection pair), not from the file geometry, so treat full-360 as an inference. The IAU landing page https://www.iau.org/public/images/detail/iau1901a/ is now 404; the ESO-hosted archive URL above works.

title: Same CE-4 farside panorama, Wikimedia Commons mirror
description: Byte-equivalent Wikimedia mirror of the IAU/CNSA CE-4 farside panorama (large JPEG).
credit: CNSA, via IAU iau1901a
licence: CC BY 4.0
notes: Dimensions/size confirmed from the Wikimedia file page text ('10,000 x 1,229 pixels, file size: 3.19 MB'), which matches my own measurement of the IAU original exactly. My direct probe of this upload.wikimedia.org URL returned HTTP 429 (rate limited) - the correct host but throttled; space out requests. Prefer the iauarchive.eso.org URL.

title: CE-4 farside panorama, full-size TIFF original

title: Yutu-2 rover leaving the Chang'e 4 lander (crop of iau1901a)
description: Cropped derivative of the IAU/CNSA CE-4 panorama showing the Yutu-2 rover on the lunar surface.
credit: CNSA, via IAU iau1901a
licence: CC BY 4.0
notes: 2185x1229 taken from the Wikimedia file page's derivative-images gallery (data-file-width/data-file-height attributes). My direct probe returned HTTP 429. Useful as a hero/foreground image rather than a full panorama.

title: Chang'e 4 lander TCAM ring-shot panorama, cylindrical projection (11 Jan 2019 CNSA release)
description: The 11 January 2019 official CNSA release of the Chang'e 4 landing-site panorama, cylindrical projection, made by the lander's terrain camera (TCAM, didixingmao xiangji). Largest surviving Chinese-media copy found.
credit: CNSA / Xinhua (Xinhua/China National Space Administration), hosted by China News Service (中新网)
licence: All rights reserved - chinanews states that use of this website's articles requires written authorisation. Underlying imagery is a Chinese government work with no explicit open licence.
notes: MEASURED by me: 206 | PNG | 960x3713 | 4372062 bytes. NOTE the file is stored PORTRAIT (960 wide x 3713 tall) - the panorama is rotated 90 degrees. Caption on the source article, quoted: '嫦娥四号着陆器地形地貌相机环拍全景图（圆柱投影）'. The original Xinhua file http://www.xinhuanet.com/photo/2019-01/11/1210035779_15471695828711n.jpg is now HTTP 404, and the china.cn copy is only 210x135. REFERENCE-ONLY: use the IAU CC BY 4.0 file (ce4-iau1901a-farside-panorama) for anything public.

title: Chang'e 4 lander TCAM ring-shot panorama, azimuthal projection (11 Jan 2019 CNSA release)
description: The same 11 January 2019 Chang'e 4 landing-site panorama released in azimuthal (disk) projection.
credit: CNSA / Xinhua, hosted by China News Service (中新网)
licence: All rights reserved - chinanews requires written authorisation for reuse. Underlying imagery is a Chinese government work with no explicit open licence.
notes: MEASURED by me: 206 | PNG | 800x786 | 521246 bytes. Caption quoted '嫦娥四号着陆器地形地貌相机环拍全景图（方位投影）', also carried by china.com.cn with credit '新华社发（国家航天局 供图）'. Azimuthal projection is a fisheye/stereographic disk - convenient for a spherical cap but not directly a skybox. Too small (800 px) for a hero asset anyway. REFERENCE-ONLY.

title: Chang'e 6 lander PCAM stitched panoramic image (CNSA, 4 June 2024)
description: Official CNSA stitched panoramic image taken with the panoramic camera on the Chang'e 6 lander, released 4 June 2024 during the far-side sample-return mission (Apollo crater, South Pole-Aitken basin).
credit: CNSA / Handout via Xinhua (People's Daily Online)
licence: All rights reserved - CNSA/Xinhua handout. No open licence stated.
notes: MEASURED by me: 206 | PNG | 1024x539 | 601444 bytes. Caption quoted verbatim from the source page: 'This stitched panoramic image released by the China National Space Administration (CNSA) on June 4, 2024, which was taken with the panoramic camera on the lander of Chang'e-6 probe, shows a view of the lunar surface. (CNSA/Handout via Xinhua)'. This CONFIRMS Chang'e 6 returned an official stitched PCAM panorama. NO LARGER VARIANT EXISTS: I probed .../mediafile/pic/SMALL/... and .../mediafile/pic/... and both return 404. Only 1024 px wide - too low for a hero panorama, and all rights reserved. The demo has no change-6 site id; adding one would need a new id.

title: Chang'e 6 lander LCAM surface images (CNSA, 4 June 2024)

credit: CNSA / Handout via Xinhua
licence: All rights reserved - CNSA/Xinhua handout.
notes: MEASURED by me (all three at 1024x752): .../20240604/17/9292031629426019497.png, .../20240604/69/6983592089598844405.png, .../20240604/92/4786878528220927460.png. Byte sizes 466665 / 609890 / 529346 respectively (from the same page scan). Companion mini-rover image at 1024x640: https://en.people.cn/mediafile/pic/BIG/20240604/15/12030254610665021119.png. REFERENCE-ONLY.

title: Chang'e 3 GRAS PCAM Level 2C colour-restored frame (2352x1728 RGB)
description: Individual Chang'e 3 rover panoramic camera (PCAM) frame, Level 2C: colour-restored, colour-corrected, 8-bit 3-band sample-interleaved RGB. One of 1,492 CE-3 PCAM products in the GRAS archive. Example frame is target sequence 056, 2014-01-13.
format: PDS3 attached label + raw binary (8-bit, 3 bands, SAMPLE_INTERLEAVED RGB)
credit: Ground Research and Application System (GRAS) of China's Lunar and Planetary Exploration Program, NAOC / CNSA. Required citation: 'This data set is processed and produced by "Ground Research and Application System (GRAS) of China's Lunar and Planetary Exploration Program, provided by China National Space Administration (http://clpds.bao.ac.cn)"'
licence: CONFLICT. GRAS copyright page states all rights reserved: '未经本平台书面许可，任何单位及个人不得以任何方式或理由对上述数据产品、服务、信息、材料的任何部分进行复制、修改、抄录、传播及销售。' BUT the National Space Science Data Center VSSO registry records the CE-3 PCAM Level 2B dataset as CC BY 4.0 (DOI 10.12176/03.03.005, CSTR 14804.11.03.03.005).
notes: MEASURED by me: 206 | application/octet-stream, resolved via the open API GET /moon-admin/client/science/dataInfo/getAnnexZip/140305090617838 which returned this plain public URL with no token. Geometry read from the file's own PDS3 attached label: RECORD_BYTES=2352, FILE_RECORDS=5187, LABEL_RECORDS=3, ^IMAGE=4 (=> 5184 image records = 3 x 1728 lines); OBJECT=IMAGE: LINES=1728, LINE_SAMPLES=2352, SAMPLE_BITS=8, BANDS=3, BAND_STORAGE_TYPE=SAMPLE_INTERLEAVED, DESCRIPTION=COLOR. IMPORTANT: the file is NOT a JPEG/PNG - it begins with ASCII 'PDS_VERSION_' followed by raw binary, so it needs decoding plus de-Bayer/calibration. This is a single frame, not a panorama; GRAS holds no mosaic/panorama product (searches for MOSAIC, PAN and kuaishi quick-view all returned 0).

The VSSO API exposes no file list, but the record's url field leads to the GRAS portal, whose UNAUTHENTICATED endpoint above enumerates all 48 CE-4 gallery items; the images serve from https://moon.bao.ac.cn/img-api/upload/... with no cookies or auth.
